html:
A Japanese film director whose work over fifty years made him one of the most influential filmmakers in the world. His films include Rashomon, Ikiru and Seven Samurai.

Born in Tokyo, he trained as a painter before joining a film studio. He made his first film, Sanshiro Sugata, a story about judo, in 1943. Rashomon, which tells one crime through the clashing accounts of four witnesses, won the top prize at the Venice Film Festival in 1951. It opened Western eyes to Japanese cinema.

He worked across many genres: samurai epics, crime films, adaptations of Shakespeare and Dostoevsky, and quiet stories such as Ikiru, about a dying official. Toshiro Mifune starred in many of his films.

His influence was enormous. Seven Samurai was remade as the Western The Magnificent Seven, Yojimbo as A Fistful of Dollars, and The Hidden Fortress helped inspire Star Wars. In later years, with Japanese studios less willing to fund him, he found foreign backers for Kagemusha and Ran, his version of King Lear. He received an honorary Oscar in 1990.
